description: 2 tactical challenges for White in the Najdorf Poisoned Pawn. After 7...Qb6 Black grabs on b2 — prove the pawn is poisoned with the famous 8.Qd2 sacrifice line.

drills.briefExplanation: 8.Qd2 Qxb2 9.Rb1 Qa3 10.f5 — White sacrifices the b-pawn for a crushing kingside initiative.
drills.description: White to play. Black has just played the provocative 7...Qb6, eyeing b2 — start the refutation with 8.Qd2!.
drills.explanation: The Poisoned Pawn variation in its most famous form. 8.Qd2 invites 8...Qxb2, and after 9.Rb1 Qa3 White has 10.f5! — opening the f-file and threatening fxe6. The main line runs 10...Nc6 11.fxe6 fxe6 12.Nxc6 bxc6 13.e5 dxe5 14.Bxf6 gxf6 15.Ne4, when White's pieces swarm: the knight heads for d6 or g5, and Black's exposed king pays for the extra pawn.
drills.name: Poisoned Pawn Accepted

drills.briefExplanation: 9.Nb3 Qa3 10.Bxf6 gxf6 11.Na4 — reroute the knight and clamp down on the queenside.
drills.description: White to play. After 8...Qxb2, try the modern 9.Nb3 instead of 9.Rb1.
drills.explanation: 9.Nb3 is White's refined alternative: rather than chasing the queen immediately, White develops and prepares Na4-c5 ideas. After 9...Qa3 10.Bxf6 gxf6 White damages Black's structure before rerouting: 11.Na4 b5 12.Nc3 eyes d5 and b5, and Black's queen remains awkwardly placed on a3 while White's center rolls.
drills.name: The Nb3 Alternative

name: Najdorf Poisoned Pawn — White Tactics
